The *Kullattheragāthā* (Thag 6.4) is a short poetic text situated within the *Theragāthā* in the Pali Sutta Piṭaka [SuttaCentral]. Falling within the *Chakka Nipāta* (the Chapter of Sixes), it comprises the verses associated with the elder Kulla. Modern translations of the text are cataloged across eight languages, including an English translation by Bhikkhu Sujato [SuttaCentral].

SuttaCentral identifies a passage-level parallel between this text and the *Dutiyasikkhattayasutta* (AN 3.90) in the Aṅguttara Nikāya, and notes that the text is cited in the *Vicayahāravibhaṅga* of the *Nettippakaraṇa* (Ne 5) [SuttaCentral]. In automated text-reuse analysis, DharmaNexus identifies 37 matching Pali passages across three works [DharmaNexus]. In post-canonical literature, extensive textual overlap occurs with both volumes of the *Theragāthā-aṭṭhakathā*, which cite and comment upon the verses [DharmaNexus]. No cross-language parallels meeting significance thresholds were detected in Chinese, Sanskrit, or Tibetan corpora [DharmaNexus].
